title: Redwood Discovery - Model Selection - Nova Systems
summary: Initial discovery focused on model selection for multi-lingual, long-context use cases and tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Customer concerned about data residency, tool-calling, and latency for real-time features. Agreed next steps: send model comparison matrix, pricing for dedicated commit levels, and schedule performance benchmark with a 32k vs 128k context test.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
action_items: Samira Patel (Redwood AE): Share model comparison spreadsheet + high-level pricing (due 2025-08-26)
Marcus Liu (Redwood SE): Provision benchmark plan and sample prompt set, include 32k and 128k runs (due 2025-08-29)
Ellen Reyes (Customer): Share POI dataset (anonymized) and list of required languages (due 2025-08-25)
next_steps: Redwood to send model/quantization recommendation doc and pricing tiers
Schedule 2-hour benchmark session (SE-led) w/ Nova infra (target week of 2025-09-01)
Customer to share compliance questionnaire and sample data subset
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-21 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Liu (Redwood SE); Ellen Reyes (Nova - Head of ML), Daniel Koh (Platform Eng), Priya Menon (Security), Marta Gomez (PM), Victor Chen (Data Scientist)

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samira from Redwood, with Marcus our solutions engineer. How's everybody doing?
[00:08] Ellen: Good, thanks. We had a quick agenda, primarily around choosing an open model for a set of features we want to launch Q4 — so multi-lingual summarization, a long-context RAG use case and some agent/tool calls.
[00:18] Marcus: Great — that's exactly the area we've been helping customers with. Before we dive in, can you outline current infra? Are you hosted on cloud VMs, do you have an internal GPU fleet, any regulatory constraints?
[00:30] Daniel: We're on GCP, primarily k8s, some internal TPU experiments but not production. For compliance, Priya here will want SOC2 alignment and audit log retention, possibly in-region data residency for EU and APAC.
[00:41] Priya: Yes, and we need KMS integration for any private deployment. Also SSO via Okta and RBAC.
[00:46] Samira: Totally understood. To frame the model discussion — are you leaning towards purely hosted API for speed-to-market, or would you consider Dedicated or Private given the residency and KMS needs?
[00:56] Marta: We want to prototype on hosted, but for production we likely need Dedicated or Private for data residency and lower jitter. Cost matters too.
[01:05] Victor: Our main functional asks: support for 8 languages — English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Mandarin; reliable tool-calling (we call external APIs to retrieve inventory), and context up to 100k tokens ideally for long doc summarization.
[01:22] Marcus: Okay, good specifics. A couple points: not all open models have robust multilingual coverage; Mistral base models are strong on English and some EU languages, Falcon tends to be strong on code and English, Llama 2 family has decent multi-lingual pretrained weights, and there are quantized variants and instruction-tuned ones. Also for 100k context, very few models support that natively — we typically evaluate 32k and 128k context model variants and use chunking/prefix KV strategies.
[01:44] Ellen: When you say 'support 128k' — is that hosted only or can Dedicated/Private handle it too?
[01:50] Marcus: Both can. Hosted has the fastest path for trials; Dedicated gives predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools and we can provision longer-context variants. Private (on-prem/VPC) is available but adds ops overhead and we'll need to validate KMS and network egress.
[02:03] Daniel: Latency vs cost — what's typical for 32k vs 128k?
[02:08] Marcus: Roughly speaking, per-token compute cost scales, and latency for a single generation with a 128k KV can be higher and needs more GPU memory. For large context workloads, batching and KV caching help but you pay for the memory and throughput. We'll send concrete numbers in the model matrix.
[02:23] Priya: On security, can Redwood Private integrate with our HSM-backed KMS? We need key import policies and audit logs.
[02:29] Samira: Yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs; we can share the security pack. For Dedicated we have KMS integrations too but the keys are still customer-managed via cloud KMS.
[02:41] Marta: About hallucinations in multilingual outputs, we're worried especially with low-resource languages — are there recommended model families?
[02:47] Marcus: For low-resource, you often see hallucination. Our recommendations: use instruction-tuned models with RLHF-style tuning if available, and maintain retrieval augmentation (RAG) with strict grounding. Mistral-Instruct variants and some Llama derivatives do better in cross-lingual tasks, but we'd want to run evals on your prompt set.
[03:04] Victor: Tool-calling — can Redwood's Hosted API do function calling or external tool orchestration? We need to call our inventory API and a DB for entity resolution, sometimes as part of a generation.
[03:13] Samira: Yes, we support function/tool calling and streaming responses on our hosted API. You can define structured output and have the runtime call external tools via our connectors or via your agent orchestrator. Marcus might add more on latency.
[03:25] Marcus: Tool-calls add a round trip; for low-latency pipelines we often run small models locally for tool selection and pass structured inputs to a larger model. Redwood supports tool-calling patterns and can route calls to internal endpoints in Private deployments.
[03:38] Ellen: Any limitations for streaming with long contexts?
[03:41] Marcus: Streaming works but with very long prefix KV the very first token latency is impacted; subsequent tokens stream normally. We'll capture these tradeoffs in the benchmark plan.
[03:51] Daniel: About model licensing — if we pick an open model like Llama derivative, are there restrictions for Dedicated/Private?
[03:58] Samira: Most open weights are available for private hosting depending on the license. We'll surface license notes in the comparison doc. For models with restrictive commercial terms we recommend alternatives.
[04:08] Marta: How do you recommend approaching quantization? We want lower cost but also minimal quality loss.
[04:13] Marcus: Quantization is a spectrum — 8-bit quant can be good for many workloads, 4-bit is more aggressive and sometimes introduces artifacts. We'll recommend quantization profiles per model and per workload in the Optimize report. For multilingual summarization, we might start with 8-bit or q4f16 and validate.
[04:29] Victor: Will we be able to pin model versions for rollouts? We need to A/B test a new instruction-tuned model vs baseline.
[04:34] Samira: Absolutely — Redwood supports model version pinning, canary rollouts, A/B testing, and automatic fallback policies. Redwood Console shows per-model metrics.
[04:44] Ellen: Can we run a POC — maybe run 32k and 128k on a subset of docs and compare latency, cost, and summary quality?
[04:52] Samira: Yes, that's a common approach. Marcus will lead the benchmark plan.
[04:56] Marcus: I'll need a representative dataset (anonymized) and a set of prompts plus expected outputs where possible. I'll run tests across a few model families — Llama-deriv instruct, Mistral-Instruct, Falcon-40B-instruct (quantized), and a 128k-capable model variant, and report token cost, p50/p95 latency, and a simple ROUGE/semantic quality metric.
[05:17] Daniel: How long does a benchmark like that usually take?
[05:20] Marcus: If we have the data and infra available, initial benchmark runs can be done in a week; deeper tuning and iteration takes longer. We'll aim to get an initial report in 7–10 business days after data and access are provided.
[05:31] Priya: For security review, we'll need your SOC2 and pen test summaries, and a list of sub-processors. Also, if we go Dedicated, who manages patching and OS-level security?
[05:42] Samira: We have SOC2 reports and pen test summaries; I'll include them. For Dedicated, Redwood manages the runtime and patching for the Redwood-managed hosts; in Private on-prem the customer owns host-level patching but Redwood supports the deployment with runbooks.
[05:56] Marta: Pricing — can you give us committed pricing for Dedicated, and burst rates? We have traffic patterns that peak weekly.
[06:03] Samira: We'll include pricing tiers: hosted pay-as-you-go, Dedicated commit levels (monthly/annual discounts), and overage/burst pricing. For predictable bursts we have burst capacity options.
[06:13] Victor: Any surprises we should watch out for with long-context model memory — like cold start times or GPU memory fragmentation?
[06:20] Marcus: Good question. Large context models can have higher cold-start times particularly for 128k due to kernel selection and memory allocation; we mitigate this with warm pools and continuous batching. We'll include warm-up guidance in the docs.
[06:34] Ellen: For evaluation metrics, can Redwood help with hallucination detection metrics and regression alerts?
[06:39] Samira: Yes — Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring, prompt-based evals, and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We'll help set up baseline evals.
[06:49] Daniel: On the networking side for Private, what about egress costs and data residency?
[06:54] Samira: Private keeps data in-region; egress depends on your cloud/provider. We'll outline networking patterns and cost implications.
[07:02] Marta: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[07:05] Samira: Recap: Redwood to send model comparison matrix with licensing and quantization notes, pricing for Hosted/Dedicated/Private, security pack (SOC2/pen test), and a benchmark plan. Nova to share anonymized dataset and language list and compliance questionnaire. Marcus to schedule bench and run initial tests.
[07:23] Ellen: Sounds good. Anything else?
[07:26] Priya: One more — can Redwood sign our DPA and do a preliminary network diagram review?
[07:31] Samira: Yes, we'll get legal involved and send draft DPA and request the network diagram.
[07:35] Victor: Cool thanks everyone.
[07:37] Samira: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links and the spreadsheet.
[52:00] (end)

Notes: transcript contains occasional mistranscriptions (product names like "Redwood Console" sometimes transcribed as "Redwood Consolee"), filler words left in. References to shared artifacts: model-comparison.xlsx (shared), security-pack.pdf (shared), benchmark-plan.md (to be created).
